name: What is the difference between a ground-level deck and a hillside deck?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a ground-level deck and a hillside deck?

acceptedAnswer.text: A ground-level deck is typically built close to the ground, requiring minimal foundation work, often just concrete footings or blocks. A hillside deck, by contrast, is elevated significantly above the ground to accommodate a slope, necessitating deeper, more robust foundations like piers or caissons, and often involves extensive structural engineering. The structural requirements and complexity are the main distinguishing factors.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ground-level decks sit low with simple foundations, while hillside decks are elevated on slopes, requiring complex, robust foundations and engineering.
